gloss: to pull out; to extract; to headhunt

definitions.explanation: to remove something by pulling it out, such as a plant, cork, or tooth
to recruit talented individuals away from another company or organization

examples.japanese: {雑草|ざっそう}を{引|ひ}き{抜|ぬ}いた。
{刀|かたな}を{鞘|さや}から{引|ひ}き{抜|ぬ}いた。
examples.english: He drew the sword from its sheath.

examples.japanese: {優秀|ゆうしゅう}なエンジニアを{競合他社|きょうごうたしゃ}から{引|ひ}き{抜|ぬ}いた。
examples.english: We headhunted an excellent engineer from a competitor.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{大手企業|おおてきぎょう}に{引|ひ}き{抜|ぬ}かれた。
examples.english: He was headhunted by a major company.

examples.japanese: {虫歯|むしば}を{引|ひ}き{抜|ぬ}いてもらった。
examples.english: I had my decayed tooth pulled out.

examples.japanese: ヘッドハンターに{引|ひ}き{抜|ぬ}きの{話|はなし}を{持|も}ちかけられた。
examples.english: A headhunter approached me with an offer to switch companies.

notes:
FORMATION:
{引|ひ}く (to pull) + {抜|ぬ}く (to extract) → to pull and extract

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive verb - takes を to mark the object being pulled out.

BUSINESS USAGE (Sense 2):
In business contexts, {引|ひ}き{抜|ぬ}き is a noun meaning "headhunting" or "poaching (of talent)." The practice is common in industries with talent shortages.

RELATED WORDS:
- {抜|ぬ}く (to pull out - simpler form)
- {引|ひ}っこ{抜|ぬ}く (to yank out - more forceful)
- ヘッドハンティング (headhunting - loanword)
